# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]

I need to figure out what these gestures mean. I have no prior context to decode them yet - I need to establish communication first, since I can't hear Mute's speech to Blind, and Blind can't see my gestures.

Let me report what I see to both Mute (who can't see it) and Blind (who can't see it), since I'm the only one who can see the bomb. I should describe it clearly. I'll wait on interpreting the gestures until I understand a scheme - but since this is turn 1 and Mute already sent gestures before I could respond, those likely relate to the manual structure (maybe numbering wire options or steps). Without an established code, I shouldn't guess wildly. Best move: report the bomb's full visual state clearly to both Mute and Blind, since Blind needs this info relayed through someone, and I need Mute to know what I see so Mute can cross-reference the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Display shows 0. Light is red. Sign embossed says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Three wires: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows 0. Light is red. There is an embossed sign that reads DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Three wires: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]

I still don't have an established meaning for Mute's gestures. Mute can't hear me confirm anything back except through speech I send to Mute (which Mute can't hear either - Mute can't hear speech, only see gestures... wait, Mute reads the manual and cannot speak or touch, but can Mute hear? Let me check: Mute's restriction is "Speak, or touch the bomb" - not hearing. So Mute CAN hear speech from others, just can't speak themselves.

So Mute can hear my speech. Good - my speak(to="mute") messages are received by Mute. Mute is communicating to me via gestures since Mute cannot speak, only gesture (and I can see gestures).

Mute sent [☝ ✌] twice now - this seems like a repeated/important signal, possibly pointing to wire 2 (index) then wire... or confirming something. Since I already told Mute the bomb state, Mute may be telling me which wire relates to a manual instruction. ☝ could mean "wire 1" or "point/first", ✌ could mean "two" or "peace/wire 2". Repeated identical gesture suggests confirmation of same message - likely indicating "wire 2" is important (✌ = 2, following a pointing gesture ☝).

I should acknowledge receipt and ask Blind to hold off, while confirming with Mute I see repeated signal.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gesture repeated: point then two-fingers. Do you mean wire number 2 is the one to cut, or wire 2 is dangerous? Confirm with thumbs up for cut, thumbs down for danger.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

Mute responded with ☝ 👍 - "point" (or "wire 1"?) then thumbs up. This could be confirming: "yes, wire 2" (thumbs up = yes/confirm) but paired with ☝ again... Actually let me reconsider: maybe ☝ isn't "point" but literally means "1". So ☝ ✌ = "wire 1, wire 2" or a two-digit reference. And ☝ 👍 = confirmation of something with a "1" reference.

Given the sign explicitly says "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE", this is critical info Mute needs, and possibly the manual has a rule like "if sign says X, do Y" that depends on display/light values. I already sent the sign text to Mute via speech, so Mute knows it. Mute's gestures might be answering a question from the manual like "what does the display show" - expecting a number relayed back, or confirming they understood step 1.

I should simplify: ask Mute a yes/no question directly to disambiguate, since gestures are ambiguous to interpret cold.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. Does the manual say to cut any wire at all?")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ 👍]

Mute responded 👍 ☝ 👍 - this could be parsed as "yes" + "1" + "yes", or "yes, [something about] 1, yes". Given my question was "Does the manual say to cut any wire at all?" a simple yes/no would just be 👍 or 👎. The extra ☝ in the middle suggests Mute is adding info: "yes, [specifically] wire 1, yes" — maybe confirming the manual says to cut wire 1 specifically, contradicting the embossed sign, or perhaps confirming the sign matches the manual (bomb sign says don't cut, manual might say something conditional).

Given the sign explicitly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and this is a strong physical warning, the safest interpretation is that the manual likely has a rule that depends on conditions (display=0, light=red) that override or confirm the sign. Mute's answer of "yes, 1, yes" might mean "yes it says something, condition 1 (display=0?) applies, yes cut" — but this is too much guessing.

I need to slow down and get unambiguous yes/no answers one at a time.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Let's go slow, one question at a time. Answer only thumbs up for yes or thumbs down for no. Does the manual instruction depend on what the display number shows?")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Clear answer: 👎 = No, the manual instruction does not depend on the display number. Good, that's unambiguous progress. Let me continue narrowing down what the manual actually says, since the sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE - I want to know if the manual agrees or contradicts.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Good, clear no. Next question, same rules. Does the manual say NOT to cut any wire, matching the sign on the bomb?")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

No - so the manual does NOT say "don't cut any wire". This means the manual likely gives a specific instruction that differs from the sign (the sign could be a red herring/trap, or the manual overrides it with specifics). Let me find out what the manual does say - likely which wire to cut, or another action entirely.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, the manual disagrees with the sign. Does the manual say to cut a specific wire?")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures: [🙏]

Mute confirms: yes, the manual says to cut a specific wire. Blind gestured 🙏 to me (or to everyone) - since Blind can't see, Blind's gesture reaches only Mute (who can see). Wait, actually gestures: "When you gesture, Mute receives it" - that's about my gestures. For Blind's gestures - Blind can't see, but can Blind gesture? Blind's restriction is "cannot see" - gesturing is a physical action, not seeing. Let me check who receives Blind's gestures: gestures are received by whoever "can see" - that's me (Deaf). So Blind gestured 🙏 and I received it (blank symbols would go to non-seers, but I can see, so I get the actual symbol).

🙏 from Blind likely means "please" or "waiting/patience" - Blind is probably waiting for instructions, prompting us to hurry up or asking for guidance.

Now I need to find out which wire via yes/no. Let me ask about wire by color/number using gestures Mute can interpret, but I need yes/no answers.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Good. I will ask about each wire, answer yes or no. Is it wire 1, the green wire?")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["🙏"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Wire 1, green, is confirmed as the wire to cut according to the manual.

Now I need to relay this to Blind, who is the only one who can actually reach and cut the wire. Blind can hear speech (Blind's restriction is only about sight and touch context - wait, let me recheck: Blind "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - nothing about hearing. So Blind CAN hear speech.

I should tell Blind directly to cut wire 1 (green), but I should also double check with Mute this is really the final instruction and not conditional on something else (like light or display, which we already ruled out only for the "any wire" question, not for wire selection).

Let me confirm no other conditions apply before instructing Blind to act - this is irreversible and critical.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed wire 1, green. Last check: does the manual instruction to cut wire 1 depend on the light color or any other condition on the bomb?")
wait()
```
